**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 19 of the MSA already lands at or above our preferred playbook position:

| Playbook element | Document treatment |
|---|---|
| Professional/workmanlike standard | ✅ § 19.1 — qualified personnel, industry standards, Order Form (reinforced by § 3.1) |
| Conformance to documentation | ✅ § 19.1 (general) and § 19.2 (period-specific) |
| Duration | ✅ 90 days from **later** of delivery or acceptance for Deliverables; Hosted Services conform **throughout the subscription term** — since "Services" is defined (§ 1.8) to include hosted software, this exceeds the 12-month software benchmark |
| Remedy | ✅ § 19.4 — re-perform/repair/replace at no charge, escalating to termination + refund of Fees; expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims |
| Compliance with laws | ✅ § 19.3 |
| No malicious code | ✅ § 19.3 (plus no functionality diminution and open-source protection for our source code) |
| Disclaimer does not swallow warranty | ✅ § 19.5 — limited to *implied* warranties, and confirms no disclaimer limits any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy |

I also checked § 21 for backdoor erosion: § 21.4 preserves caps on failure of an exclusive remedy but does not designate § 19.4 as a sole remedy, and § 6 acceptance mechanics support rather than limit the warranty trigger (payment, silence, or productive use needed for testing is not acceptance).

The one small narrowing is the malicious-code warranty covering code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" rather than an absolute no-malicious-code commitment. That carve is market-standard and, against an otherwise above-preferred warranty package, not worth spending negotiating capital on — so I did not raise a redline.
